title: “You Owe It To Yourself”
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The post holds up the phrase "You owe it to yourself" as a small but powerful tool for leaders. Many hard-working people put others' expectations first and need someone with standing to give them permission to attend to their own well-being and goals. The author argues the phrase signals care, builds confidence, affirms self-worth, and nudges people out of their comfort zone. Leaders are encouraged to say it to themselves first and then to use it deliberately with team members, colleagues, and friends.
points: Leaders can give people permission to prioritize their own needs by using a simple, caring phrase.
The statement works because it comes from someone who evidently cares about the listener.
People are often so fixated on others' expectations that they forget their own best interests.
Leaders should apply the idea to themselves before offering it to others.
quotes: These hard-working team members, colleagues and friends need a leader to remind them that sometimes it is okay to focus on their own needs and goals rather than putting others first.
Because it comes from a leader, it suggests they have a right to pursue what is good for them without fear of evaluation.
The statement empowers others because it suggests they have earned the right to honor themselves.

This simple expression boosts confidence, acknowledges a person’s self-worth, encourages the other party to make choices that align with their true desires, pushes them to take a step outside their comfort zone, and reminds them that the investments they have made shouldn’t be taken for granted.
Before addressing others, good leaders direct this expression at themselves, giving themselves permission to find personal happiness and satisfaction in what they pursue.
